designs.approach:
ROUTE AT THE WINDOW PROCEDURE, one upstream hook in Tree. Tree.callWindowProc gets one recipe-inserted block. It sits right after the hwndParent/hwndHeader early returns, before the WM_SETFOCUS switch and before the pre-switch that turns WM_SETREDRAW off for WM_VSCROLL. The block hands every message aimed at the content plane (viewport != null && hwnd == handle) to a new per-Tree TreePlaneRouter. The router answers four kinds of message and returns TreePlaneRouter.PASS for everything else, so all other traffic keeps today's path.

(1) TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE is always answered on the logical rows. The viewport never sends it: it moves the plane only with resetPlaneTop's TVM_SELECTITEM/TVGN_FIRSTVISIBLE, and onVScroll uses wmScroll(update=true) on hwndParent. So every TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE that reaches the plane is external: TreeDropTargetEffect's auto-scroll, or Tree's own stock space-key and Ctrl-key paths, which are still active in viewport mode. The handle is mapped through VirtualTreeResidentPlan.entryOf/keyOf and TreeViewport.rowOfKey to its visible row, and answered with the TreeView semantics TreeViewport already implements (ensureAncestorsExpanded, then VirtualTreeViewport.ensureVisible + layout). It returns TRUE only when it scrolled and nothing expanded. A handle that is not a resident row returns FALSE and never reaches comctl32.

(2) WM_VSCROLL sent to tree.handle (a client, or Tree's Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown) applies the TreeView's line/page/top/bottom/thumb steps to the logical top. The bar follows, and the rows coming into view paint inside the call. Scrollable.wmScroll still sends the vertical ScrollBar's Selection event afterwards, exactly as stock.

(3) TVGN_CHILD is never faked globally. The viewport's own residency walks (childrenLaidOut, detachSubtree) need the native truth, and so do Tree's stock code paths that are live in viewport mode: TVN_ITEMEXPANDING's runExpanded test, DI_GETDRAGIMAGE's getSelection walk and createTreeItem. Instead, the external sender declares its query. A one-statement recipe hook in TreeDropTargetEffect.dragOver sends a registered message (SWT_M3_DROP_CHILD_QUERY, lParam = hovered row) right before its TVGN_CHILD test. The router consumes that declaration on the next TVGN_CHILD (one-shot, keyed by handle). When the TreeView has no native child but the logical row has a known child count > 0 (which is exactly when a stock row has native children after SetData), it answers the row's own live handle as a non-zero token; stock dragOver only tests != 0. The viewport's two own TVGN_CHILD sends are moved to OS.CallWindowProc (Tree.TreeProc, ...), so they never pass the router: own versus external is structural, not a flag.

(4) A TVIS_DROPHILITED TVM_SETITEM to a non-resident handle is dropped, so a remembered dropIndex can never reach comctl32 after its row was freed.

Exactness around the router lives in TreeViewport:
- The TVIS_DROPHILITED row is captured in the existing captureResidentState loop and kept resident as an anchor in nativeWindow, the same way the caret is, so the effect's dropIndex keeps naming the same row.
- Tree.setInsertMark gets one hook that makes the insert mark a lane (item + side), re-applied after each window commit.
- The resident window always includes one edge row above the top and one below the last full row (the partial row), even when memory pressure takes the overscan to 0. The native TVGN_PREVIOUSVISIBLE/NEXTVISIBLE the effect asks are therefore always the logical neighbours.
- The parent-window bar copy follows official 3.135.0 (javap). TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE is not an updateScrollBar point, so the shown bar is kept. createItem/destroyItem while drawing are update points, so item-count changes refresh the bar. By analysis this reproduces all eight official DndFeedbackOracle lines (up follows because new roots get SetData with setItemCount; down-after-up stays at 96; expand gives 103/339 and 7/339).

Allocation: none per dragOver. The router uses one int[6] scratch per Tree and plan lookups are open-addressing.

Donor-first: no third-party code. Reused in-repo precedents:
- List.callWindowProc WM_VSCROLL routing and ListViewport.onVScroll steps and 32-bit thumb.
- TreeViewport.showItem/ensureAncestorsExpanded (EnsureVisibleOracle).
- nativeWindow's caret anchor.
- The Display/IME RegisterWindowMessage pattern.
Wine comctl32 treeview.c is pattern-only (LGPL), and the authority is the official-jar oracles. The implementer must append the T7 rows to docs/m3/tree-viewport/FOSS_REUSE_DECISION.tsv (via foss_reuse_decision.py) before writing code.

The plane stays as it is. The design adds a viewport-aware drop-effect path and keeps the stock path unchanged.

1. Hooks in TreeDropTargetEffect: two METHOD_START delegations, in dragOver and dragLeave. dragEnter only resets fields and needs no hook. Each delegation passes a plane tree to a new package-private class, org.eclipse.swt.dnd.TreeDropTargetViewport. That class is an ADAPT copy of the stock effect: same fields, same hysteresis values, same hit test, same TVIS_DROPHILITED writes, same insert mark. It replaces only the three native steps that do not hold on a content plane:
   - Auto-scroll: stock reads native neighbours (TVGN_PREVIOUSVISIBLE/NEXTVISIBLE), which at the window edge are overscan or anchor rows. It then sends TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE, which scrolls the plane behind the viewport (the measured getItem(Point) desync). The new path moves the logical top instead.
   - Auto-expand: stock tests TVGN_CHILD, but a collapsed plane row has no native children. The new path asks the logical model.
   - Writes to a remembered native row: the new path checks the handle is still resident before writing, because handles of retired rows are reused.

2. Cross-package access: a new internal bridge, org.eclipse.swt.internal.ViewportDropFeedback, in the win32 source folder. It follows the VisibilityGate Port pattern: public final, @noreference/@noinstantiate, with a nested abstract Port that the widgets package installs once. It offers four allocation-free queries. Without a port, or for a tree that is not a plane, each answers the way the stock code assumes:
   - plane(tree)
   - autoScroll(tree, hItem), which returns stock's 'scroll' flag
   - hasChildren(tree, hItem)
   - resident(tree, hItem)

   The port is widgets.TreeViewportDrop. It is installed from TreeViewport's static initializer, which runs at the first Tree.createWidget. It answers from TreeViewport over logical rows:
   - rowOfHandle = plan.entryOf + rowOfKey.
   - The stock scroll decision uses logical previous/next rows. The stock label-rect test is measured natively on the resident next row, so x-dependence is kept.
   - dragEnsureVisible gives TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE semantics on the logical top: VirtualTreeViewport.ensureVisible, then layout. There is no native scroll and no synchronous paint.

   Rejected alternatives:
   - Public @noreference methods on Tree: they add API to an upstream class and put logic in Tree.java.
   - M3RowMath public API: it has no viewport-mode query, and visibleItem materializes and pins facades.

3. Bar parity. In a tree whose visible bar is stock's parent-window copy (stockParentWindow, plus columns or a measured scrollWidth), TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE moves the TreeView's own bar but never reaches SWT's updateScrollBar. The copy therefore stays as shown. The design models this with a third bar state, copiedBar, separate from the existing staleBarRow/frozenBar (which model a stale own bar). copiedBar is released only where stock copies again:
   - Tree.updateScrollBar reached from stock code: callWindowProc's key/scroll/size/mouse/font/timer messages, TVN_SELCHANGED, TVN_ITEMEXPANDED, setRedraw.
   - Item creation or destruction mediated by the viewport with drawing on (stock createTreeItem/destroyItem).
   - Every existing barFollowsTop/clearStaleBar site.

   This reproduces all 8 DndFeedbackOracle rows. For example, MeasureItem at top 100 holds 96/299 on the way down, because the rows entering were already filled. At top 0 the bar follows, because SetData of new roots calls setItemCount(40), which creates items. The ExpandBarOracle rows (focus and selectVisible keep 7/339) are untouched.

4. Client WM_VSCROLL to tree.handle: one Tree.callWindowProc hook, placed before the switch that turns redraw off (List.java:324 precedent), calls TreeViewport.onPlaneVScroll. That applies the TreeView's scroll steps to the logical top: barFollowsTop, itemHeightKey, setTopRow, paintNow. Scrollable.wmScroll still sends the ScrollBar Selection event, as in stock. SWT's own Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown, which sends SB_PAGEUP to the handle, now scrolls as in stock.

5. Original mode: tree.viewport is null. The hooks return false without allocating, the stock bodies run, and every TreeViewport change is reachable only through viewport.

Allocation per dragOver matches stock: 3 Points, TVHITTESTINFO, TVITEM on a highlight change, and the same findWidget. A scroll step (at most one per 200 ms rest) costs one window commit, the same as one wheel notch.

Verdict on the angle (make the plane answer like a complete TreeView, with TreeDropTargetEffect.java left byte-identical: blob 182a1cd8d7ee, no hook). Paths are relative to S:/m3-scratch/worktrees/swt-name-convergence. Code was read at 2dcbcb50f1; HEAD later moved to 5bf82c5d38, with changes to docs and tools only.

(A) QUERIES are answered natively and made exact by what the resident window guarantees. This is FEASIBLE. The queries are TVM_HITTEST, TVGN_FIRSTVISIBLE/PREVIOUSVISIBLE/NEXTVISIBLE/CHILD, TVM_GETITEMRECT with GetClientRect, TVM_SETITEM with TVIS_DROPHILITED, and TVM_SETINSERTMARK.
- A1, neighbour rows: an overscan floor TreePlaneProtocol.NEIGHBOUR_ROWS=2 per side, set through a new opt-in VirtualTreeViewport.requireOverscanRows that only TreeViewport.install calls. adaptiveOverscan can return 0 under heap pressure (VirtualTreeViewport.java:99). With the floor, top-1, the partial row top+visible and the row after it are always resident.
- A2, native first child: TreeViewport.rebuild calls the existing common Residency.addExpanderHints (VirtualTreeVisibleProjection.java:62-71; GTK prior art, gtk/Tree.java:1663). Every resident, materialized, collapsed row with known children gets its LOGICAL first child as a hidden native child, keyed (row,0).
  - The plan reuses that handle when the row expands, so there is no reinsert and the delta gate is untouched.
  - TVGN_CHILD therefore answers like stock.
  - The hint carries child 0's facade id when one exists, so there is no phantom facade.
  - A hint first needed while SetData runs is deferred to beforePaint, so there is no TVM_INSERTITEM inside TVN_GETDISPINFO.
- A3, pins: captureResidentState also reads TVIS_DROPHILITED and tree.hInsert. nativeWindow keeps those rows native as anchors, generalising the caret anchor at TreeViewport.java:598-612. The handles the effect remembers (dropIndex, insertItem.handle) are therefore never retired or recycled while in use.

(B) SCROLL REQUESTS: TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE and client WM_VSCROLL.
- Converting native plane scrolls after the fact is INFEASIBLE as the mechanism:
  - The TVS_NOSCROLL plane does not scroll for either message. FirstVisibleProbe.output.txt shows 'after TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE root 49 first visible=root 0'. NoScrollProbe is cited in TREE_MEDIATED_VIEWPORT.md:44. ExpandBarOracle lineDown shows nothing happening on the M3 jar. So there is nothing to convert, and this is why the M3 jar never scrolled in DndFeedbackOracle.
  - The plane's only native moves are resets to its first root (FirstVisibleProbe: expand or collapse above) and the unexplained MeasureItem desync (getItem(Point) row 3 answered root 94). Neither is a stock scroll, so converting them would invent scrolls.
  - Clearing TVS_NOSCROLL per call, as resetPlaneTop does for TVGN_FIRSTVISIBLE, would:
    - re-show the plane's own bar, needing SWP_FRAMECHANGED per step;
    - compute page, thumb, top, bottom and the end clamp over the resident window instead of the logical rows;
    - blit and double-paint.
- Instead, the requests are pre-empted at the native seam. One recipe hook at the top of Tree.callWindowProc lets TreeViewport claim both messages before the redraw pre-switch, as List.callWindowProc:324 already does for the List viewport.
- TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE becomes VirtualTreeViewport.ensureVisible of the handle's logical row: to the top from above, to the bottom from below, nothing when the row is fully visible. A hidden target goes through showItem's ensureAncestorsExpanded path.
- The bar follows stock's copy rule. Where stock has a parent window, SWT copies the TreeView's bar only in updateScrollBar (Tree.java:7665). TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE is not a copy point, so the bar as shown before the scroll is written back after the logical layout, and the next updateBar (any layout or Tree.updateScrollBar) ends it. This reproduces the official MeasureItem data:
  - up-steps 99..96: the entering top row's SetData calls setItemCount, which lays out (stock: createTreeItem copies, Tree.java:3493);
  - down-steps hold 96 with top 97..100, because those rows are cached and nothing copies.
- WM_VSCROLL becomes TreePlaneProtocol.vscrollTarget, then barFollowsTop and setTopRow. The bar follows because stock's post-switch updateScrollBar copies: ExpandBarOracle lineDown goes 7/339 to 1/339. Scrollable.wmScroll then sends the ScrollBar Selection event exactly as stock (Scrollable.java:592-595).

(C) After-the-fact detection is kept only as a guard. Before each TVM_HITTEST, the plane's first visible row is compared with what resetPlaneTop last achieved, and a moved plane is pinned again (planeRepins counter, DEBUG log; the gate expects 0). It re-pins and never converts.

Rejected alternatives:
- Synthetic TVGN_CHILD answers, fake or self handles: comctl32 handles are pointers, and detachSubtree :858, childrenLaidOut :439, Tree.nativeFirstChild :312 and TVN_ITEMEXPANDING :9775 walk them, risking a crash or a loop.
- Non-logical placeholder rows: Tree._getItem(h,-1) at Tree.java:268 would mint phantom facades, and they would show when the row is expanded.
- Answering TVGN_ROOT, TVGN_LASTVISIBLE, TVM_GETCOUNT or GetScrollInfo(tree.handle) like the full tree: impossible for a windowed plane. GetScrollInfo is user32 and never reaches the window procedure. The effect uses none of them.

Layout of the change:
- New logic goes in the new file TreePlaneProtocol.java (pure, no native call, no allocation), with glue in TreeViewport.java (our own file).
- VirtualTreeViewport gets the opt-in floor.
- Upstream Tree.java gets exactly one hook. TreeItem, DropTarget and the effect are untouched.

Cost per dragOver:
- A hysteresis-only dragOver gets one int test per message and one TVM_GETNEXTITEM per hit test, with zero allocations.
- A scrolling dragOver (at most one per 200 ms) runs one viewport layout, the same as any wheel scroll today.

strengths: Stock dragOver/dragLeave keep running unchanged in viewport mode. The only addition is one declared registered message before the TVGN_CHILD test at TreeDropTargetEffect.java:223, so future upstream fixes still apply. With -Dswt.widget.mode.Tree=original, M3_DROP_CHILD_QUERY is 0 and dragOver sends exactly the stock message sequence.

The bar-copy model rests on official bytecode, which I checked in t7snap/official/Tree.javap.txt: createItem(TreeItem,...) runs getDrawing() at 722-726, then updateScrollBar at 730. TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE is not an update point.

keepBarAsShown runs after layout(). That is correct, because layout clears stale bars whenever the top row changed (TreeViewport.java:214 with barShapeChanged comparing layoutTopRow at :249). Traced against dnd-oracle-l.tsv, it reproduces all 8 official lines: up 99..96 refreshed by SetData→setItemCount→itemsChangedBar, down holds 96/299 while the top goes 97..100, top=0 down follows 1..4, expand 103/339 and 7/339 via barAfterExpansionInView, and leave unchanged.

TVGN_CHILD is never faked globally. The answer is one-shot and keyed by handle. The viewport's own sends at :439 and :858 go through CallWindowProc(TreeProc), so runExpanded (Tree.java:9775), DI_GETDRAGIMAGE (7883) and createTreeItem (3379) keep the native answer.

H1 sits after the hwndParent/hwndHeader returns (2632-2637) and before the WM_SETREDRAW-off pre-switch (2692-2700). M3InsertStatements can place it: the anchor matches the squeezed prefix and is unique. WM_VSCROLL keeps Scrollable.wmScroll's Selection event (Scrollable.java:592-595). paintNow matches the wheel's synchronous repaint. Tree's own space and Ctrl TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE paths also become logical.

Robustness extras: a drop-highlight anchor reusing the captureResidentState loop, an insert-mark lane that also keeps marks set on non-resident items, edge rows for the neighbours, and a guard that drops DROPHILITED writes to non-resident handles.

Its evidence holds up. Cited lines check out. It spotted that the setRedraw hook is in the yml (316-322) but missing from gen_tree_viewport_yml.py. It plans a discriminator oracle that could falsify its own copy model, plus a ClientVScrollOracle.

Cleanest original mode. TreeDropTargetEffect.java stays byte-identical, Tree.java gets one hook guarded by viewport != null, and VirtualTreeViewport's floor is default-neutral (Math.max(Math.min(0,cap), adaptive) equals adaptive). Viewport mode runs the stock dragOver verbatim.

TVGN_CHILD becomes stock-like because collapsed rows get real hidden native children from the existing Residency.addExpanderHints (VirtualTreeVisibleProjection.java:62-71, used by GTK at gtk/Tree.java:1663). The design rejects fake handles, avoiding the crash and loop risk in native walkers. The NEIGHBOUR_ROWS=2 floor keeps top-1, the partial row and the row after it resident even when adaptiveOverscan returns 0 (VirtualTreeViewport.java:99).

TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE and WM_VSCROLL are pre-empted before the redraw pre-switch, the same placement as List.java:324. The anchor 'long hItem = 0;' is unique: the WM_SETFOCUS case's 'long hItem = OS.SendMessage' does not match the squeezed key.

The held bar is written back after layout(), so official 96/299 on the way down holds (cached rows trigger no SetData and no layout). SetData-driven layouts refresh it 99..96 on the way up. The copy lag stays outside the model's expand-in-view stale state, and any later updateBar ends it, including Tree.updateScrollBar copy points such as the first WM_MOUSEMOVE after the drop. That is closer to stock after the drop than a frozen bar.

parentCopyLags (stockParentWindow && (columnCount != 0 || scrollWidth != 0)) matches stock's real copy condition (Tree.java:7665, scrolledHandle 6030), so header-only trees follow, as stock's own TreeView bar does.

The TVM_HITTEST guard re-pins a moved plane before every hit test, with a planeRepins counter the gate expects to be 0. This protects DnD hit testing against the MeasureItem desync whatever its trigger. Pins keep the dropIndex and hInsert handles valid. The design is candid about unknowns: the NULL-item TVGN_NEXTVISIBLE empty strip, NO_SCROLL trees, page and thumb rules, and paint timing.

fatal: The bar-copy hold breaks on the very oracle line it targets. dragEnsureVisible sets copiedBar before calling layout(). layout() runs `if (barShapeChanged ()) clearStaleBar ();` (TreeViewport.java:214), and barShapeChanged compares topRow with layoutTopRow (:249), so it is true after any scroll. The design's change (c) makes clearStaleBar null copiedBar, so the held copy is discarded inside the same call and the bar follows the top. Official measure=true top=100 down0..3 (96/299 while the top goes 97..100) would show 97..100 instead. This contradicts the design's own claim that it reproduces all 8 oracle rows and its JUnit expectation.

Regenerating m3-swt-tree-viewport.yml with gen_tree_viewport_yml.py ('never hand-edited') silently drops the existing setRedraw hook. That hook is in the yml at 316-322 but absent from the generator's TREE_HOOKS. Dropping it removes `viewport.redrawEnabled ()` (Tree.java:6663), so setRedraw no longer brings back the bar or adopts the item height (ExpandBarOracle and HeightBarOracle setRedraw cases). check_tree_hooks_present.py reads the regenerated yml, so it would not flag the loss.
strengths: Original mode is exact. The METHOD_START delegations return false when tree.viewport == null and send no extra native message, including for non-viewport trees in a viewport-mode JVM. The WM_VSCROLL hook is guarded by viewport != null.

Its bar model is conceptually the most faithful: copiedBar is a separate state from staleBarRow/frozenBar, released only at stock updateScrollBar points and at item create/destroy. stockBarCopy uses stock's exact copy condition (columns or scrollWidth, Tree.java:7665).

Scroll neighbours and the child test come from logical rows (rowOfHandle, hasLogicalChildren), so no fake native answers are needed. The scroll-step logic mirrors stock 184-208 for top 0, the empty area and the last row. Allocation matches stock.
It handles licensing honestly: the derived mirror keeps the IBM EPL-2.0 header, and the ledger rows cover the GTK row-index hysteresis and the HiDPI PRs.

verdicts.recommendation:
Ranking under STOCK FIDELITY: route 7.5, plane 7.0, effect 3.5. Neither route nor plane has a fatal flaw. Tracing the code, both reproduce all 8 DndFeedbackOracle lines and keep the original mode stock. Effect, as written, fails the late-bar-copy lines.

Take route as the base and fold in three things from plane:
1. The TVM_HITTEST re-pin guard with its planeRepins==0 gate.
2. The exact copy condition parentCopyLags (columns or scrollWidth). Route's stockParentWindow() wrongly holds the bar in header-only trees, where stock's own TreeView bar follows.
3. Plane's separation of copy lag from expand-in-view staleness. Route reuses frozenBar for both, so Tree.updateScrollBar copy points (WM_MOUSEMOVE, TVN_SELCHANGED, TVN_ITEMEXPANDED) never release a DnD-held bar, and a stale thumb outlives the drop. Route acknowledges this. Alternatively, adopt effect's copiedBar idea, but assign it after layout().

Pin page step, thumb and synchronous paint for WM_VSCROLL with ClientVScrollOracle. Route and effect paintNow, plane does not. The wheel precedent at TreeViewport.java:1264-1269 suggests stock repaints synchronously. Also run route's discriminator case (roots 90..99 pre-painted) before admitting itemsChangedBar.

Plane is the purer choice for original-mode identity: TreeDropTargetEffect stays untouched. But its hint rows change native structure for every viewport tree: TVN_ITEMEXPANDING runExpanded (Tree.java:9775), TVM_EXPAND notifications, VK_MULTIPLY recursion and native counts. The keys, plain, presentation and NativeWork differentials must stay green before it is preferred. Its held bar is a raw SetScrollInfo that any non-copy layout erases, for example a wider MeasureItem row reaching setScrollWidth, which calls viewport.layout at Tree.java:6755.

Desync evidence: the measured root 94 matches exactly a plane whose first visible row was reset to its first native row. That row is the caret anchor root 0, which shell.open gives the caret at top 0, followed by roots 92, 93, 94. This is consistent with TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE moving the TVS_NOSCROLL plane by a reset rather than a one-row scroll. Plane's citation of FirstVisibleProbe does not settle the point: that probe's top was already root 0 before the TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE line. All three designs remove that trigger from the DnD path; only plane guards against any other cause.

Reject effect as written:
- copiedBar is cleared by layout()'s barShapeChanged→clearStaleBar in the same dragEnsureVisible call, so official 96/299 on the way down becomes 97..100.
- Regenerating the yml drops the setRedraw hook.
- The mirrored IBM dragOver will drift from upstream.
- Tree's own TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE senders still move the plane.

strengths: Every TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE and WM_VSCROLL that reaches the plane is answered on the logical rows before the WM_SETREDRAW pre-switch (Tree.java:2692-2700). That covers the effect (TreeDropTargetEffect:206) and also Tree's own live senders: WM_CHAR space (7999), Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown sending WM_VSCROLL (8253/8273) and the Ctrl+arrow TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE (8282). Verified: TreeViewport never sends either message to the plane. The only hits are comments at 1190/1267/1572/2032/2250/2566, and onVScroll uses wmScroll on hwndParent (992). So the claim that the router only ever sees external senders holds.

Native TVGN_CHILD answers stay true. The router answers on the logical rows only for a query the sender declared, once, keyed by handle. The viewport's own sends (childrenLaidOut 439, detachSubtree 858) move to CallWindowProc(Tree.TreeProc), which is package-private at Tree.java:136. Tree's live consumers stay native: runExpanded (9775), the DI_GETDRAGIMAGE getSelection walk (4958) and createTreeItem's TVGN_CHILD(-1) (3379). Nothing can run between H4 and line 223, so the declared query cannot be stolen.

Handles the effect remembers stay valid. The drop-highlighted row is read in the same TVM_GETITEM loop captureResidentState already runs (2637) and is kept native as an anchor, like the caret (598-612). The router drops DROPHILITED writes and TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE for handles that are not in the plan, using O(1) plan.entryOf (VirtualTreeResidentPlan:70). The insert mark becomes a lane that is re-applied after each window commit. Today detachSubtree zeroes hInsert (851) and the effect never re-sends it for the same facade.

Edge rows make the native PREVIOUSVISIBLE/NEXTVISIBLE of the top row and the last full row the logical neighbours even when adaptiveOverscan returns 0 (VirtualTreeViewport.java:99). They are computed inside TreeViewport, so the shared VirtualTreeViewport used by the original virtual Tree (Tree.java:3685) is not touched. At the default overscan of 8 the window is unchanged (ViewportRuntime paintStart/paintEnd 152-165).

Parked and empty planes are safe: the router answers 0 for handles that are not resident, dropId is reset when the plan is empty, and resetPlaneTop already returns early on an empty plan (875). Original mode is gated by viewport == null (Tree.java:3690) and by M3_DROP_CHILD_QUERY == 0, which uses the same expression as TreeViewport.ENABLED (45).

All anchors resolve in the recipe engine as claimed. 'if (hwndHeader != 0 && hwnd == hwndHeader)' is unique. The TVGN_CHILD anchor at line 223 is reached through the else branch, because M3InsertStatements.insertBelow descends into else parts (224-229). A constructor works as beforeMethod: the yml already uses 'beforeMethod: Tree'.

Strongest guarantee that the plane stays in sync with the viewport. TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE and WM_VSCROLL are pre-empted before the redraw pre-switch, at anchor 'long hItem = 0;' (2673). That anchor is unique: the WM_SETFOCUS 'long hItem = OS.SendMessage' squeezes differently. On top of that, a pinnedTop-versus-TVGN_FIRSTVISIBLE detector re-pins the plane at TVM_HITTEST and counts planeRepins. This still works if the desync trigger is something other than TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE, and the trigger is unproven.

An overscan floor of 2 rows, kept inside the per-side cap and opt-in only from TreeViewport.install, keeps top-1, the partial row and the row after the partial row resident. That last row is the case route's edge rows leave uncovered.

The DROPHILITED row and the tree.hInsert row are pinned as anchors (a generalisation of the caret anchor at 598-612) and released together with their facades in releaseFacades. Remembered handles cannot be recycled. A TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE for a handle that is not in the plan returns 0 without a native call.
Cleanest original-mode identity: TreeDropTargetEffect is byte-identical, Tree.java gets a single hook guarded by viewport != null, and nothing else outside the viewport's own files changes.

The expander hints reuse in-repo prior art: Residency.addExpanderHints (VirtualTreeVisibleProjection:62-71, used by gtk/Tree.java:1663). They are keyed (row, 0), so the resident plan reuses the hint's handle when the row expands, and the delta gate does not regress.

fatal: As written, the bar hold never survives a scroll step. dragEnsureVisible sets copiedBar = shownBar() before v.ensureVisible(row) and layout(). layout() calls clearStaleBar() whenever barShapeChanged() (TreeViewport.java:214), and barShapeChanged() compares topRow since commit 2dcbcb50f1 (line 249). The design itself extends clearStaleBar to null copiedBar. So every step shows the new top: the MeasureItem top=100 down rests read 97..100/299 where official 3.135.0 reads 96/299 (dnd-oracle-l.tsv), and the design's own DndFeedbackOracle gate fails.

TreeDropTargetViewport mirrors IBM's EPL-2.0 dragOver/dragLeave and must carry an EPL-only IBM header. This contradicts the programme rule that new logic goes into Synexia-headed Apache-2.0 OR EPL-2.0 files, and NTPRA. Because the METHOD_START hooks skip the whole stock body in viewport mode, upstream fixes to dragOver would silently stop applying to viewport trees.
strengths: The plane's native message semantics do not change: the viewport's own TVGN_CHILD/NEXT/ROOT sends and every stock TVGN_CHILD consumer stay native, and no router runs on every message.

The scroll decision uses logical neighbours: rowOfHandle is plan.entryOf plus rowOfKey, and next is row + 1. Overscan rows and caret-anchor rows therefore cannot pose as neighbours in the normal case. Auto-expand reads the lanes (materializedChildId, childCountKnown, childCount) and never returns a fake handle.
Scroll and expand work runs in the effect's own frame, not inside a native message answer. That makes it the design with the least re-entrancy into the window procedure during dragOver.
Writes through a remembered dropIndex (in dragOver and dragLeave) are checked with plan.entryOf before they reach comctl32, so a freed handle is never written.
The WM_VSCROLL hook sits before the redraw pre-switch (List.java:324 precedent), so redraw is never left off. Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown therefore page logically.

verdicts.recommendation:
Take route as the T7 base, with three fixes before merge.

1. Make the edge rows reach one row past the partial row, or move plane's 2-row floor into TreeViewport's windowFirst/windowCount. At overscan 0 (VirtualTreeViewport.java:99) with a caret anchor below the window (nativeWindow 598-612), resting on the partial row makes TVGN_NEXTVISIBLE return that anchor. The router then answers TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE by jumping the logical top to the caret instead of stock's two-row step.

2. Add plane's pinnedTop detector, at least as a counter and gate. Re-pin only outside SetData and paint (Tree.java:2848-2853 warns against scrolling there). The desync mechanism is unproven:
   - The m3 measure=true 'root 94 at row 3' decodes to a plane reset to its first root: the caret anchor root 0 (from beforeSetFocus), then roots 92, 93, 94 with overscan 8. A one-row native scroll would not give that.
   - FirstVisibleProbe's 'after TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE root 49' line started with the first visible already at root 0 and targeted a row below the view. It says nothing about the ensure-visible above the top that the up-rest sends.
   - So route's and effect's causal claim (TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE caused the desync) and plane's counter-claim (the plane never scrolls) are both unverified.

3. Release frozenBar at stock updateScrollBar points: the callWindowProc post-switch (2795) and TVN_SELCHANGED (9695). As designed, the drag leaves the bar frozen at 96/299 while the top is 100, and it stays that way after the drop until a key, the wheel or a scroll.

Reject effect.
- Its bar hold is broken (copiedBar is captured before the layout that clears it), and its mirrored IBM file conflicts with the header and licence rule.
- It leaves the plane exposed to Tree's own native TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE plus TVM_SELECTITEM TVGN_CARET: WM_CHAR space (7999) and Ctrl+arrows (8282). Ctrl+Up on the top row of a MULTI tree moves the plane natively and no layout follows to re-pin it, so later hit tests miss.
- It keeps no anchor for dropIndex or hInsert. If a DragOver listener moves the window farther than the overscan, a reused HTREEITEM equal to dropIndex leaves the hovered row without a highlight (mirrored lines 241-258 skip both the clear and the set). The insert mark also stays lost while the same facade is hovered.

Do not adopt plane's expander hints in this leaf.
- They change TVGN_CHILD for every collapsed row with known children. That touches the viewport's own walks (439/858) and Tree's runExpanded (9775), and roughly doubles native rows.
- They make 'resident' handles hidden: rowOf/attachRow bind child 0's facade to a hidden hint row.
- Hints created during SetData are deferred to the next paint. With no repaint, or with setRedraw(false) during the drag, auto-expand silently stops.
- They turn setNativeExpanded's TVM_EXPAND into a full native expansion. Its TVN_ITEMEXPANDED is handled regardless of ignoreExpand (Tree.java:9783-9793) and runs expansionChanged→layout re-entrantly inside TreeViewport.setExpanded, before refreshLogicalRange and restoreTop (2180-2183). In the DnD case that happens inside the effect's dragOver.
- Its guard runs resetPlaneTop (a style toggle plus SWP_FRAMECHANGED) inside arbitrary TVM_HITTEST senders.

strengths: All four hooks checked with the real recipe engine (M3PerFileApply on scratch copies). Each lands where the design says: callWindowProc after the hwndHeader early return, setInsertMark before 'hInsert = hItem;', the field before the TreeDropTargetEffect constructor (same pattern as Tree's viewport field, beforeMethod: Tree), and the statement before the nested TVGN_CHILD test at dragOver:223. The second pass reports UNCHANGED.

It found real recipe drift. Regenerating gen_tree_viewport_yml.py today drops exactly the 7-line setRedraw entry, which I confirmed by diffing a regenerated copy against the committed yml. The design syncs the generator and also adds DeclarativeRecipesTest bindings, an ACCEPTANCE row, a checker --dnd option and a correction-ledger row.

No new public API. The dnd-to-widgets link is a registered window message (the same pattern as Display/IME RegisterWindowMessage), and every new member is package-private. The logic sits in a new TreePlaneRouter with the Synexia header.

Routing allocates nothing: one int[6] scratch array per Tree and open-addressing plan lookups. The H4 statement runs only when the expand timer fires. In original mode M3_DROP_CHILD_QUERY is 0, RegisterWindowMessage never runs and no extra message is sent.

The fix for TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE and WM_VSCROLL is on the receiving side, so it covers every sender: DnD, Tree's own space and Ctrl-key paths, and clients. Tree's own TVGN_CHILD walkers stay native. Documentation comes before code (T7_PLANE_ROUTING.md, ASPECT_MATRIX, FOSS rows).

The hooks use the programme's standard shape: one-line METHOD_START delegations in dragOver and dragLeave, plus a WM_VSCROLL guard modelled on List.java:324. All are confirmed to land where claimed and to reach a fixed point. Upstream footprint is 3 statements.

It is the only design that wires TreeDropTargetEffect.java into tree_viewport_cycle.sh's M3PerFileApply passes and into the presence checker. Today the cycle passes only Tree.java and TreeItem.java, and the checker reads only those two.

In original mode, and for trees without a viewport, the stock body runs untouched with no extra native message. Allocation parity can be tested: a ThreadMXBean bytes-per-call gate compares the two modes, and the JUnit class runs in both.
Most new logic goes into new files. The derived file keeps the IBM EPL-2.0 notice and adds Synexia as contributor, as brief rule 8 requires for donor-derived code.

The oracles are promoted to docs/m3/tree-viewport/evidence/oracles with stock recordings. The JUnit class name matches viewport_gate.sh's _Viewport selector. copiedBar is an explicit bar state with named release points.

Smallest upstream footprint: one guarded statement in Tree.callWindowProc before 'long hItem = 0;', confirmed to land there with a fixed point. TreeDropTargetEffect stays byte-identical (blob 182a1cd8d7ee confirmed), and TreeItem and DropTarget are untouched.

The fix is on the receiving side and works for any sender. The plane answers TVGN_CHILD, TVM_ENSUREVISIBLE and WM_VSCROLL for the stock effect, subclasses and clients alike, which fits brief rule 25 (we own the implementation).

No new API. Decisions live in a new pure TreePlaneProtocol (no native call, no allocation) that can be unit-tested without a display. Answers reuse SCROLLINFO fields, so nothing is allocated per answer.

It reuses existing in-repo prior art: common Residency.addExpanderHints (already used at gtk/Tree.java:1663) and the caret-anchor pattern. The overscan floor is opt-in with a default of 0, so GTK and the original virtual Tree are unchanged.
Documentation comes first (T7 row in the design doc, FOSS ledger rows), and the oracles are promoted to evidence/oracles with stock recordings.

verdicts.recommendation:
Ranking under this lens: plane 7, effect 6.5, route 6. No design has a fatal flaw under this lens.

**How the hooks were checked.** I applied every design's hook rows with the real M3PerFileApply engine to scratch copies in K:/codex-work/agent-temp/claude/e--ws2-com-synexia/a6de83fe-6489-4056-8689-f1217602e9cc/scratchpad/t7judge (scratch yml, copies, a replica of the checker). Every anchor exists, lands where claimed, and the second pass reports UNCHANGED.

**Recommended: plane's shape**, meaning one receiver-side hook, the DnD file untouched and no API. It needs four fixes:
1. Its row belongs in gen_tree_viewport_yml.py TREE_HOOKS, not in a hand-edited yml. tree_viewport_cycle.sh:12 regenerates the yml before applying it, so a yml-only row is erased. Add the missing setRedraw row in the same change; regenerating today drops exactly that entry (confirmed by diff).
2. Hold the parent-window bar copy through the bar model, using route's keepBarAsShown/frozenBar or effect's copiedBar. A raw SetScrollInfo is silently overwritten by the next updateBar.
3. Make the hit-test guard a gate counter rather than a production re-pin. It is a side effect inside claimsPlaneMessage and adds one native TVGN_FIRSTVISIBLE per TVM_HITTEST, including the item-tooltip WM_MOUSEMOVE findCell path.
4. Treat the expander hints as the main maintainability risk. They change the native window and stock TVGN_CHILD walkers (runExpanded at Tree.java:9775, VK_MULTIPLY) for every viewport tree, so land them only behind the NativeWork, keys and expand differentials.

From effect, borrow the oracle promotion, the ThreadMXBean allocation gate and the checker/cycle wiring.

**Effect.** It has the most standard hooks and the best harness wiring, but:
- Its ~150-line IBM mirror copies the DPI hit-test line. Upstream changed that line 4 times since 2024, most recently pointToPixel to pointToPixelAsLocation in f51bb3b4c4.
- ViewportDropFeedback is a public internal bridge that the other two designs show is avoidable.
- It adds a third bar state.
- It skips the design-doc and ASPECT_MATRIX update.
- Its claim that the regenerated yml contains only additions is wrong: regeneration drops the setRedraw hook.

**Route.** It has the best generator hygiene and the deepest analysis, but:
- It has the largest upstream footprint. Its four hooks include a Synexia message protocol and a RegisterWindowMessage field in the IBM DnD file, plus a setInsertMark hook that plane shows is avoidable.
- M3AddMemberIfMissing drops H3's trailing //$NON-NLS markers, so the design's own check_tree_hooks_present --dnd gate reports H3 as MISSING. I reproduced this.
- The cycle script still passes only Tree.java and TreeItem.java, so H3 and H4 never land through the documented cycle.
- Its oracles stay in the session scratchpad instead of docs/m3/tree-viewport/evidence/oracles.

**Minor.** viewport_gate.sh only selects test classes ending _Viewport or _ViewportDifferential. Effect's test class is picked up; route's and plane's are not.
